newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Empire rescues shares, denies takeover.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Empire rescues shares, denies takeover.

text.p: Property firm Empire East Land Holdings Inc's revelation on Wednesday that it had bought back over six million shares provides only part of the reason why the stock has surged in the past two days, analysts said.
The oversold state of property issues as well as rumours the company was being taken over by a businessman with deep pockets also helped Empire's rise, they said.
Empire closed 50 centavos, or 15.63 percent, higher at 3.70 pesos on Wednesday in a second-day surge. Together with Tuesday's rise, the stock has risen by 90 centavos, or 32 percent.
Empire announced on Wednesday that it bought back late on Tuesday 6.356 million shares at three pesos each.
The buy-back boosted the share, Asiamerit Securities vice-president Teresa Lee said.
Talk in the market said the money for the buy-back was lent by a Filipino-Chinese tycoon, who would take over the company.
"If ever there is such a takeover by a tycoon with deep pockets, that would be positive for the company," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
The rumour was denied by Empire East president Gerardo Garcia.
"If there is any takeover that is being done, I am not aware of it. We are not talking to anyone. Probably people are now starting to realise that there is value in the company," Garcia told Reuters.
Officials of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, Empire's parent firm, were not immediately available for comment.

Shares in Empire and Megaworld have been hammered in recent weeks by rumours of banckruptcy and a meltdown in the Philippine property sector. Both companies repeatedly denied they were facing financial trouble.
Empire dropped to an all-time low of 2.70 pesos early this month from an initial public offering price of 12.90 pesos.
"It is the underdog stock perhaps for the decade. It is now adjusting to its true value," said Guoco's Mejia.
Brokers said an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission on possible price manipulation in Empire and Megaworld stocks could also augur well for the issues.
"People may be realising that there's nothing bad about the company and that it is doing well," said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.

"More and more investors are probably seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and that rumours which weighed down the issue are just rumours," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
Sun Hung Kai securities vice-president for research Raul Ruiz said at its present price, Empire's price earnings of 3.8 times made the issue one of the cheapest in the property sector.
